name: Narcissus Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Sakhalin to japan; winters to philippines and borneo
description: Small flycatcher. Adult male is splendidly colored with a glowing orange supercilium, throat, and breast set against black upperparts, white underparts, and a white wing patch.

name: Cape Gannet
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off southern africa; disperses to coastal mozambique
description: Gregarious, strong-flying seabird. Adults are whitish with an apricot-colored head; note also the distinctive blackish arrow-shaped tail and pointed dark wingtips and hind wing.

name: White-chested Swift
rangeDescription: Lowlands to mid-montane forest and openings from northwestern colombia southward through western amazonia to northwestern bolivia
description: Rare and poorly known. A fairly small swift, all black with variable white patch on chest.

name: Chestnut-breasted Partridge
rangeDescription: Coniferous foothill forest of sikkim to southeastern tibet
description: Ornate partridge of east Himalayan foothill forests. Often in areas with dense bamboo stands.

name: Western Citril
rangeDescription: Highlands of eastern democratic republic of the congo to uganda and northern zambia
description: Small seedeater with a sharp bill and forked tail. The upperparts are olive-green and the underparts pale yellow with some sparse streaking.

name: Bates's Swift
rangeDescription: Humid forest of western cameroon to northern gabon and eastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A small, entirely blackish swift with a slightly dusky throat and a deeply forked tail. Flies rapidly over lowland forest, occasionally gliding briefly.

name: Beautiful Sunbird
rangeDescription: Mauritania, senegal, and guinea-bissau eastward to sudan, eritrea, and ethiopia, southward to sierra leone, central nigeria, northern cameroon, central african republic, south sudan, extreme northeastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, and northwestern kenya
description: A slim, long-billed sunbird in which breeding males and females are very different. Breeding males are mostly dark green with a red-and-yellow band across the underparts.

name: Malabar Parakeet
rangeDescription: Southwestern india (western ghats)
description: This striking parakeet is restricted to the forests of India’s Western Ghats. Bluish-gray male has a bright red upper bill and a black-and-blue collar.

name: Tanganyika Masked-Weaver
rangeDescription: Swamps of southwestern tanzania (karema to rukwa) and zambia
description: A typical red-eyed masked-weaver with a plain olive-green back and pink-brown legs. The breeding male has a black face mask extending midway up the forehead, surrounded by a strong burnt-orange wash that spreads to the breast and flanks.

name: Hoffmanns's Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Southern amazonian brazil south of the amazon river to rondônia and southern mato grosso
description: Large woodcreeper with a strong black bill. Dark chestnut-brown overall.

name: Cameroon Mountain Greenbul
rangeDescription: Montane forest of nigeria and cameroon
description: A medium-sized greenbul of the mountains of Cameroon and southeastern Nigeria. Remarkably uniform yellow-olive in plumage, with a red eye.

name: White-cheeked Cotinga
rangeDescription: Andes of western peru (la libertad to ayacucho)
description: Rare cotinga found only in high-elevation woodland in the western Andes of Peru. It is heavily streaked with brown and buff and has a white face and black cap.

name: Large Hawk-Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Breeds from northern pakistan to india through indochina, southern china, and taiwan; winters to southern india (eastern and western ghats), bangladesh, lowlands of the thai-malay peninsula, greater and lesser sundas, and philippines
description: This species’ maddening song can be likened to the phrase “brain-FEVER,” which adequately describes what this bird gives birders trying to see one as it sings high up in the forest canopy. If seen well, note hawk-like appearance, with a long barred tail, brown upperparts, and patterned white underparts.

name: Flores Minivet
rangeDescription: Western lesser sundas (sumbawa and flores)
description: A small, long-tailed songbird that perches upright. Male is largely black with white underparts, a contrasting red breast patch, red wing markings, and a red rump and outer tail feathers.

name: White-bellied Dacnis
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to southern venezuela, northeastern peru, and central amazonian brazil
description: Small, handsome tanager with piercing yellow eyes. Males are mostly cobalt-blue with a white belly and a black mask.

name: Spot-winged Rosefinch
rangeDescription: Himalayas (garhwal to nepal and sikkim)
description: Rather large rosefinch of the Himalayas. Male is dark pink with broad pale eyebrows and two rows of fine white specks on the wings.

name: Marsh Babbler
rangeDescription: Northeastern india (arunachal pradesh to cachar, khasi, and chittagong hills)
description: A small, mostly brown bird with a heavily streaked pale breast. Note the white eyebrow, the white throat, and the rusty flanks and belly.

name: Olive-tree Warbler
rangeDescription: Balkan peninsula and türkiye; winters in eastern and southeastern africa
description: Large warbler with long wings. Pale olive-gray overall with whitish underparts.

name: Ashy Antwren
rangeDescription: Andean foothills of western bolivia (la paz, cochabamba, and santa cruz)
description: Scarce antwren found in Andean forest mainly in Bolivia, but also known from a few remote locations in southern Peru. Male is plain gray; female is brown with a faint gray tinge to the crown.

name: Sri Lanka Drongo
rangeDescription: Western sri lanka
description: Large, upright, blackish bird with a long, deeply-forked tail and tuft of feathers on the forehead. Typically found in pairs, often in mixed flocks, within the understory of humid forests in the lowlands and foothills of Sri Lanka’s Wet Zone.
